blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Universe encompasses all space, time, matter, galaxies, and celestial bodies originating from the Big Bang.
The Milky Way Galaxy houses our Solar System, which is centered around the Sun.
Planets are classified into Inner (Terrestrial) and Outer (Jovian) planets based on their distance and composition.
Natural satellites like the Moon, along with dwarf planets, asteroids, and comets, form other vital celestial components.
Memorizing individual planetary features and the order of planets is crucial for SSC and competitive exams.

blocks.content: The Universe is the vast, infinite space that contains everything that exists. It includes galaxies, stars, planets, satellites, asteroids, comets, dust, and gases. The Universe has no definite shape or boundary and is continuously expanding.

The Big Bang Theory is the most accepted theory regarding the origin of the Universe. According to this theory, the Universe originated from an extremely hot and dense point called a singularity. A massive explosion occurred, after which the Universe started expanding. This expansion is still continuing.
A galaxy is a huge system of billions of stars, planets, gases, and dust held together by gravity. There are billions of galaxies in the Universe.

blocks.content: The Milky Way is the galaxy in which our Solar System is located. It is a spiral galaxy and contains billions of stars. The Sun is one of the stars of the Milky Way galaxy.
Stars are massive, self-luminous celestial bodies that emit heat and light. They produce energy through nuclear fusion reactions occurring in their core.
The Sun is a medium-sized star and the central body of the Solar System. It is composed mainly of hydrogen and helium. The Sun provides heat and light to all the planets of the Solar System.

blocks.content: The Solar System consists of the Sun, eight planets, their satellites, asteroids, comets, meteoroids, and other celestial bodies. All planets revolve around the Sun in elliptical orbits.

rows: Few or no moons, no ring systems
Numerous moons, presence of ring systems

blocks.content: The eight planets in order from the Sun are:

items: Mercury
Venus
Earth
Mars
Jupiter
Saturn
Uranus
Neptune
Mercury: Closest and smallest planet. No atmosphere and no satellite.
Venus: Hottest planet due to greenhouse effect. Rotates from east to west. Called Earth's twin.
Earth: Only planet known to support life. Has water, oxygen, and suitable temperature. Called Blue Planet.
Mars: Known as Red Planet due to iron oxide. Has two moons – Phobos and Deimos.
Jupiter: Largest planet and gas giant. Has maximum number of satellites.
Saturn: Known for its ring system. Least dense planet.
Uranus: Rotates on its side due to extreme axial tilt.
Neptune: Farthest planet from the Sun. Strong winds and very cold.

blocks.content: Dwarf planets are celestial bodies that orbit the Sun but have not cleared their orbital path. Important dwarf planets include Pluto, Ceres, and Eris. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
Satellites are celestial bodies that revolve around planets. They can be natural or artificial.

items: Sequence of planets from the Sun and their relative sizes are frequently asked in SSC exams.
Specific planetary aliases (e.g., Venus as Evening/Morning Star, Mars as the Red Planet) are high-yield questions.
Key facts about the Moon, solar/lunar eclipses, and satellite data are recurrent exam topics.

blocks.content: The Moon is the only natural satellite of the Earth. It has no atmosphere and no water. The Moon reflects sunlight and causes tides on Earth.

items: Asteroids are rocky bodies found mainly between Mars and Jupiter.
Comets are made of ice and dust and develop a tail when they come close to the Sun.
Meteors burn in the Earth's atmosphere and are called shooting stars.
Meteorites are meteors that reach the Earth's surface.
